35 stations (81–114 plus 109B), in printed order. Section: WEST COAST OF SCOTLAND.

How I copied things:
- Fragments are each line with its leading indentation removed; the spacing inside the line is kept as printed. In "other" I've labelled the column values (schedules, returns, Values, Feet) so you can tell them apart. The printed tokens themselves are unchanged.
- Trailing commas stay on names (and on the place, where there is one), following your "Farn, Inner," example. Where a locality follows the name (Ushenish, N. Uist; Rona, Skye; Kyleakin, W. Ross; Lismore, Oban; Fladda, Easdale; Skerryvore … Tiree; Pladda/Lamlash, Arran; Turnberry, Ayrshire), I split it into name and place. "Stornoway (2 Lights)," stays whole as the name.
- No keepers, types (L.H./L.V.) or light characters are printed in this list. Line 2798 points to "Diary from the Stations." for the reporters' names, so keepers is [] for every row.
- I couldn't interpret the "Values" column (roman numerals I–VI). It isn't explained here, so I've only copied it.

Sub-headings: only two are printed, "Sutherland" (81–82) and "Outer Hebrides" (from 83). Every later row technically sits under "Outer Hebrides", so that's what I gave as coast. But from 89 (Rona, Skye) onward the stations are on the mainland or Inner Hebrides and down the Clyde to Galloway, so the heading clearly stops applying. It looks like intermediate sub-headings were left out or lost.

Oddities worth checking:
- 84 Stornoway: the Values cell is a braced pair, "{ II. }" with "{  I. }" on the next line (2814), one value per light. Feet is 56 for both.
- 86 Monach Islands: there's a stray opening brace before "I." with nothing matching it.
- 92 Ardnamurchan has no Feet. 105 Sanda has no Values or Feet.
- 109B Ailsa Craig: printed "Ailsa Craig, 1885" with no Values or Feet, and no * even though it shows 3 schedules filled in 1887 and 1 year of returns. "1885" is probably a start date, but I can't tell what it refers to (I believe the light was first lit in 1886).
- 109 Turnberry has a * (returned in 1887) but 0 schedules filled in 1887. That's a contradiction in the print.
- 103 Lochindaul: 8 schedules in 1887 but only 4 years of returns. That's possible, just worth noting.
- 93 Skerryvore wraps onto line 2824, and Values and Feet are on that second line.

Spellings as printed, not corrected: Rhu Stoir (Stoer), Island Ghlais (Eilean Glas), Dhuheartach (Dubh Artach), Lochindaul (Loch Indaal), Mull of Cantyre (Kintyre), Devaar (Davaar), M'Arthur's Head. The list says "Monach Islands" but the Diary below says "Monach Isles". The Diary also gives keepers for this section, e.g. Robert Agnew at Butt of Lewis and Joseph Agnew at Monach Isles.
